Executive structural synthesis

Spain's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as mixed structural picture. Growth Quality: Broad-based growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Broad competitiveness deterioration. Household Demand: Durable-led discretionary demand. External Sector: External drag on growth. Across the five modules, 2 are favourable, 1 mixed/neutral and 2 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 20.7% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 47.0% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 52.2%. Total real GFCF growth was +5.1% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: High intellectual-property share; Strong real GFCF growth.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as broad competitiveness deterioration. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q2), real labour productivity per hour grew -0.1% year-on-year versus +0.8% in EU-27. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +3.5% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Non-positive productivity growth; Elevated NULC growth.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as durable-led discretionary demand. Real household consumption grew +3.3% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 7.3% of nominal household expenditure and services for 62.7% in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Strong services consumption growth.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as external drag on growth. Net exports contributed -0.60 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Exports contributed +0.10 pp and imports -0.70 pp. Real exports grew +0.3% YoY while real imports grew +2.1% YoY. Watchpoints: Domestic demand accompanied by import drag.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
